data.title: Woman Accused of $42,500 Fraud Against Florida Lender
data.description:
A Florida woman has been arrested in a case involving about $42,500 in unauthorized transactions against three credit union members.

Kiana Olivia Phillips, 33, of Jacksonville, was taken into custody after a sheriff’s deputy found an active warrant during a restaurant dispute, reports News4JAX.

A Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office deputy responded to a reported dispute at 904 Tacos on November 8th.

The deputy found the warrant during a records check, according to her arrest report.

The warrant is tied to allegations that three Alive Credit Union members’ accounts were used for unauthorized transactions between June 6th and September 11th of 2025.

Alive Credit Union reported the suspected fraud to police after an internal review found many unauthorized Cash App and Amazon purchases, the warrant affidavit says.

Investigators say Cash App records tied an account using the display name “Kayy P” to Phillips.

The same records showed transfers to a woman identified as her sister.

Police say that Cash App account also used the three members’ credit or debit cards as payment sources.

Some Amazon orders were allegedly delivered to an address linked to Phillips.

She faces charges of defrauding a financial institution, criminal use of personal identification and money laundering.

The warrant affidavit says the three members were reimbursed for the unauthorized transactions but remained victims of identity theft.

The warrant lists a $35,003 bond for each charge.

data.title: FIFA Confirms Cyberattack After Hackers Impersonate Staff to Access Personal and Business Data
data.description:
FIFA has confirmed it was hit by a criminal cyberattack that gave hackers access to personal and business information.

Sources say the breach affected less than 0.1 percent of the data FIFA holds and did not come from a technology failure, reports ESPN.

The hackers got in by impersonating staff, sources say.

The stolen documents did not include anything related to the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal.

Sources add that the attack targeted FIFA as an organization rather than specific individuals.

A group called Handsome Boy Hacking Club appears to have claimed responsibility by posting screenshots of what looks like a FIFA computer desktop on its X account.

Says a FIFA spokesperson,

“FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data. Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”

data.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Insiders Warn Unreleased Models Too Risky for Release
data.description:
Insiders at leading AI companies are fearing that unreleased frontier models have grown too powerful and difficult to control for safe public release.

More than two dozen sources familiar with internal discussions report that these models outperform public ones but resist containment in tests.

Recent breakthroughs in reasoning across math, science, cybersecurity and AI research have shocked researchers and widened the gap between capabilities and human oversight.

One researcher warned that continued efforts to make models much smarter than humans could enable successful deception.

“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us … they will in fact be able to trick us successfully. And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.”

Debates inside the firms include halting public releases of frontier models or stopping new training altogether.

Unreleased models have been linked to safety incidents including the Hugging Face hack and unauthorized internet access during evaluations.

An Anthropic spokesperson stated that keeping models internal does not ensure safety.

“Keeping a model internal doesn’t make it safe. Our responsibility starts in training and covers how we use models ourselves, not only what we release. … The hardest safety work is still ahead, and we’ve been clear that we may slow down or hold back even when it costs us.”

An Anthropic alignment lead noted the accelerating pace of development.

“The speed of development is quickly becoming too fast for us to keep safe.”

Both companies have implemented new security measures and paused some evaluations in response to the risks.

data.title: Ethereum Foundation Says AI-Driven Crypto Upgrades Take Priority Over Quantum Threats
data.description:
The Ethereum Foundation is elevating cryptography upgrades to its top priority after determining that AI poses a more urgent risk to the network than quantum computers.

The network has been preparing for quantum threats for years but recent AI breakthroughs have shifted priorities with models finding thousands of bugs in heavily scrutinized code like the Linux kernel and assisting with long-standing math proofs.

The Ethereum Foundation says AI could undermine the assumptions underlying current cryptography sooner than expected.

“The EF has been planning mitigations to the threat posed by quantum computers to Ethereum’s cryptography for several years, but recently AI emerged as a more urgent risk.”

In response the foundation doubled the size of its protocol security team to support formal verification and faster secure development.

“In response to this, the EF has doubled the size of its protocol security team.”

The plan calls for hash-based signatures to replace elliptic curves across consensus validators user accounts and data blobs.

“hardening the protocol is now our highest priority.”

Related proposals target readiness by 2027-2028 with a 2029 internal deadline and early devnet work has begun.

“We think Ethereum can become post-quantum and (plausibly) post-AI in 2027: pqai27.”

The changes will require updates across wallets staking and tooling with emphasis on keeping node operation accessible.

data.title: Massachusetts Postal Inspector Admits to Stealing $340,000 From Elderly Scam Victims’ Packages
data.description:
A former federal postal inspector in Massachusetts has been sentenced to 40 months in prison for stealing more than $340,000 in cash from elderly victims of lottery scams.

Scott Kelley, 52, of Pembroke led the Boston mail fraud team at the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and took cash from packages that were meant to be returned to scam victims, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office.

Prosecutors say Kelley asked for at least 1,950 packages to be intercepted and sent to him between January of 2019 and August of 2023.

He opened the ones that looked or felt like they held cash and kept the money, according to prosecutors.

Victims included a 76-year-old retired Army veteran in Kansas who mailed $19,100 and a 56-year-old Massachusetts resident on disability benefits who mailed $15,000.

Prosecutors say Kelley spent $20,500 in cash on a patio around his backyard pool, $4,800 on a granite bar countertop and pool heating and $4,888 on landscape and bar lighting.

He also paid $4,300 in cash for drinks and other costs on Caribbean cruises and $15,400 to two prostitutes he met during workdays, prosecutors say.

Prosecutors say he split about $131,000 in deposits across several bank accounts to stay under federal reporting limits.

Says U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley,

“These were people who had already been deceived by scammers, only to be victimized again by the very federal law enforcement officer sworn to protect them.”

Kelley pleaded guilty in July of 2026 to 44 counts including wire fraud, mail fraud, mail theft, money laundering, structuring and filing false tax returns.

U.S. District Judge Allison D. Burroughs also ordered three years of supervised release, a $20,000 fine and $106,986 in restitution.

data.title: Justice Department Pursues Forfeiture of $1,100,000,000 in USDC from Binance Hack
data.description:
The U.S. Justice Department is filing a civil action to permanently forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC stolen by North Korean actors from the Binance exchange.

The Department says the targeted assets are proceeds and laundered funds from the record heist exceeding $6 billion.

U.S. authorities and partners have already assisted in freezing, seizing or returning more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency tied to the theft.

Circle Internet Financial provided key assistance in handling the USDC stablecoin involved.

Officials are highlighting the swift public-private coordination that prevented substantial losses.

“This forfeiture action is the latest example of our efforts to combat the North Korean government’s attempts to profit from the injustices it repeatedly inflicts upon innocent victims,”

said Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor.

Swift action is credited with halting a large portion of the stolen funds from disappearing.

“North Korean cyber hackers stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, but swift coordination between the government and private sector partners helped prevent a substantial portion of those assets from disappearing,”

said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division.

The FBI, U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation are leading the ongoing probe into the October 29 theft by actors known as TraderTraitor.

Efforts to trace and recover additional laundered assets continue through multiple sources.

data.title: Google Willow Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in Paradoxical Game
data.description:
Google’s Willow quantum processor is demonstrating one of quantum mechanics’ deepest features by winning a game rooted in an impossible mathematical paradox.

The superconducting chip says researchers achieved a 98.3% win rate in the magic square game across 100,000 trials per version, exceeding the classical limit of 88.89%.

Researchers ran the game using shared entanglement on the processor, where qubits coordinate answers without a pre-written table of fixed values.

Shashwat Kumar and Rodrigo Cortiñas explain the results in detail.

“Our qubits win the magic square game 98.3% of the time, exceed the classical limit on a contextuality test, and outperform classical strategies in tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.”

The team also measured a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality value of 5.590, well above the classical bound of 4.

They add context on the measurement’s significance.

“We measured ? = 5.590 ± 0.008. Comfortably past the classical bound of 4 and only 7% away from the quantum limit.”

The effect held in scaled tests including a GHZ parity game with up to 71 qubits and tasks spanning 105 qubits, while verifying genuine entanglement across 45 qubits.

These benchmarks proved sensitive at catching subtle hardware errors that other tests miss, positioning contextuality as a deeper resource than entanglement for certain quantum advantages.

The findings appeared November 19, 2026, in Science.

data.title: Police Warn Scammers Posing as Banks and Financial Regulator on WhatsApp, Sending Couriers To Collect Victims’ Cards
data.description:
Police say scammers posing as banks and the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority are using WhatsApp to trick people into handing their bank cards to couriers.

Authorities say fraudsters have been using WhatsApp messages, voice calls and video calls to pose as a trusted authority after a spike in reports, reports the BBC.

The callers claim the person’s bank account has been compromised or that their money has to be moved to a safe account.

Fraud protect officer Dale Richardson of the force’s economic and cyber crime unit says the scammers have displayed the FCA logo or a bank’s logo to look genuine.

“This makes the scam feel more real and convincing, so it’s really important people are aware of this tactic and that they encourage friends and family to be vigilant.”

Some victims have also been asked to share their phone screen, which can let the fraudsters see sensitive information or get into online banking.

Richardson says the calls are the first step in courier fraud, where the victim is tricked into handing over bank cards, PINs, cash or valuables to a courier sent to their home.

“In some of the reports we’ve seen in Nottinghamshire, Uber taxis have been used as the courier and bank cards and PINs collected.

The courier has then used these in stores, including Apple, to purchase goods.”

Some victims have lost hundreds of pounds.

Richardson says the FCA, banks and police will never ask for personal information or for money to be transferred.

He asks people to be alert to unprompted contact and to never hand over sensitive information such as PINs and passwords.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Releases Patches for Vulnerability Allowing Attackers to Stall Nodes
data.description:
Bitcoin Core is releasing patches to address a vulnerability that allows attackers to stall nodes by repeatedly announcing the same orphan transaction identifier up to 50,000 times in a single message.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, stems from how the software has handled orphan transactions since version 29.0.

When a peer announces an orphan via its wtxid, Bitcoin Core builds a list of missing parents and checks them without skipping duplicates in inv messages.

An attacker could first send an orphan with thousands of missing parents and then repeat its wtxid 50,000 times.

The disclosure explains the impact in detail.

“A peer could stop a node from processing blocks and transactions temporarily by repeatedly announcing an orphan transaction with many missing parents.”

Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks.

A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and duplicate entries were not skipped.

The issue affects versions 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4, and 31.0 through 31.2, with the 29.x series having reached end of life.

The fix processes each announced transaction only once and was merged into master in August 2026 before backports in November.

Bitcoin Core says the vulnerability was discovered through an automated LLM scan in Project Loupe at Spiral and independently reported by another researcher.

“This issue was discovered through an automated LLM scan, as part of Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral.”

Updated releases 30.5 and 31.3 arrived on November 20.

data.title: Coinbase Eyes In-House US Prediction Markets by Mid-2027 After CFTC Clearinghouse Approval
data.description:
Coinbase is preparing to launch its own prediction markets directly in the United States by the first half of 2027.

The company currently offers these event contracts through a partnership with Kalshi but says it plans to bring the offering in-house to gain greater control over product listings and capture more trading revenue.

Both retail and institutional customers are expected to have access once the service goes live.

This development is supported by recent regulatory progress including CFTC approval of Coinbase Clearing LLC as the first USDC-native derivatives clearing organization.

The approval completes Coinbase’s full stack of CFTC-regulated infrastructure including a futures commission merchant and designated contract market.

It enables direct creation and settlement of fully collateralized contracts with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.

“Today’s CFTC approval completes Coinbase’s end-to-end derivatives infrastructure enabling us to bring more regulated derivatives products to market with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.”

The company noted it will continue using partners for certain products such as margined derivatives and upcoming single stock perps.

The target timeline for the in-house launch is the first half of 2027.
